comments.text: The code at $C138 and $C455 writes rows directly into the VIC sprite area beginning at pointer $09.

Writable digit sprite images. Rendering the glyphs at $7F4C gives the visible digit shapes, which are copied into columns of these images.
Sprite slots $32 and $33 around the HUD score display, with pattern bytes copied from $C4E0 by $C5E4.
Middle row byte of the first HUD graphics slot, written with the sprite's three-byte stride.
$C5E4 writes this last byte of each row of the $0C80 HUD marker.
First byte in each row of the $0CC0 marker sprite.
The second byte in each row of the sprite at $0CC0, updated by $C5E4.
Sprites $34-$3B start with a pickup marker, four title banner sections and the Game Over and Bonus Scene sections.
$C5A5 copies custom glyph data into this byte column of sprite $34, advancing three bytes for each row.
Rows inside the $38 sprite slot, the fourth and final section of the title banner. The raw NMI vector in the stopped handoff image happens to target this address.
Trailing rows of the Game Over first section, followed by the second section and the first Bonus Scene section.
Second Bonus Scene section and first ending text section. $75F9 copies both sprite slots to $1F00 before scene setup.
The final two slots show the trailing half of the ending message and a mushroom.
Six character codes per tile, in three-column, two-row order. $7D04 chooses a page by the tile range and uses tile times six modulo 256 as its offset within the page.
Six character codes copied into $1EF4-$1EF9 at scene setup.
First character of the stage-dependent tile, copied from the source at $867F.
Second character and solidity input tested by the handler at $C168.
Third character of the tile patched by the code at $96CC.
Fourth character of the tile, written by $96CF.
Fifth character of the tile, written at $96D2.
Final character code of this tile's six-byte definition. Scene setup can replace this portion of the character lookup.
First cell on the second row of tile $2A. The retained disk utility can overwrite it by stepping through a self-modifying target page.
Continuation of the six-byte tile-character table. This address begins at the second character on the first row of tile $35.
Entry chooses character $2B for this tile cell. The alternative disk reset path assigns another value at the same address.
Start-up code selects character $2B for this tile definition cell.
Character-code entry written by $7617 and the disk reset path, followed by the definitions for the next tiles.
The start-up replacement for this cell of the six-byte tile table, followed by the other cell definitions.
One of the tile-character bytes redefined by the entry code at $7621. Subsequent bytes are part of the third page of six-byte tile definitions.
Tile character replaced with $CE at start-up. This part of the table covers late tile IDs.
Entry patches the final character in this tile definition to $2B.
First character of the secret gate's six-byte definition. $B8C1 reads it and $B8EE can change it.
Second character of the secret gate, set to $34 by the graphics change at $B8F3.
Third character byte of tile $7E. The secret transition gate at $B90F requires it to equal eight.
Temporary copy made by the start-up at $75F9. Alternate scene setup restores it to $0EC0 before rewriting the interlude graphics.
Two sprite slots used side by side to draw the Best Time lettering.
VIC sprite slots beginning at pointer $80. These include the 200 and 100 labels, star shapes and several object shapes. $2025 and $2065 also receive regenerated numeral rows.
Byte position for row 1 of the digit copied by $9DA1 into VIC sprite $80.
Byte position for row 2 of the digit copied by $9DA1 into VIC sprite $80.

Beginning of the $84 image slot. This region includes the paired flickering shapes, thin branch shapes, vehicle-shaped objects and two star silhouettes in $8E and $8F.
VIC image pointers $90-$9F include the rock in $91, small pickups and blocks of character animation.
VIC image pointers $A0-$AF include the curved-torso and head profiles and sets of creature poses.
VIC image pointers $B0-$BF include four hedgehog frames at $B4-$B7 and four shell shapes at $B8-$BB.
VIC image pointers $C0-$CF. The walking animation at $9760 selects left and right sets from $C8-$CF.
VIC image pointers $D0-$DF include Terry's weapon poses, the yo-yo components, two spark shapes and the 1000-point label.
Begin sprite pointer $DB. The pickup test treats this image as the kind counted toward an extra life.
Slots $DC-$DF include the balloon-shaped image, a small speckled frame and two related object poses.
VIC character bitmap base. Each of the 256 codes takes eight bytes. The two observed matrix settings $1F and $2F share this charset.
Row byte at $384B cleared by entry code and restored to $20 by an alternate reset path.
Eight bitmap rows for character $17, used as the seed for the visible phase at $C1A2.
Bitmap rows beginning at code $33. The copy at $C444 addresses this part of the character graphics.
The eight source bitmap bytes copied to $3FD8 for tile $4D before the object spawn.
Character rows for codes $80-$FF, including bytes changed by the tile animation routines. $C686 writes the three dynamic slices starting at $3CB8.
First of three writable slices of the animated character art, filled from $C656.
This eight-row cell is cleared in the scene setup loop before the phase renderer runs.
Second slice populated by the phase renderer from $C666.
Eight rows cleared by the scene initialization loop as part of the dynamic art reset.
The third slice populated by the phase renderer from $C676.
The bitmap for character $9C is cleared in scene setup. Later addresses continue the playfield character set.
Beginning of character $E7 in the VIC charset. The animation routine at $C307 writes into the surrounding glyph data.
Writable tile bitmap refreshed by $C192 from the $38B8 seed.
Writable glyph for the spawn tile, filled when $C147 accepts contact and tested by $C15F.

Third of four phase-dependent bytes in the glyph slice.
Last of the four bytes patched per table entry by $C1F1.
Writable character bitmap with its eight rows cleared by the level initializer.
Writable rows updated in $C222 from its phase table.
The final eight rows of the playfield charset, initially cleared when scene rendering is reset.
Low bytes of fourteen resident map stream addresses, indexed by scene. Combine each with the corresponding high byte at $4010.
High bytes paired with $4000. Scenes 8 through 13 index streams in RAM beneath KERNAL ROM.

Packed bytes for normal scene 02. This span starts at tile row 1 and runs through row 7; the stream continues to $4A6A.
Packed bytes for normal scene 02. This span continues inside tile row 7 and runs through row 12; the stream continues to $4A6A.
Packed bytes for normal scene 03. This span starts at tile row 1 and runs through row 9; the stream continues to $4FFC.
Packed bytes for normal scene 03. This span continues inside tile row 9 and runs through row 12; the stream continues to $4FFC.
Part of the third regular scene's packed stream, whose bounds are $4A6B-$4FFC. The IRQ vector in the stopped handoff image still points here.
Packed bytes for normal scene 04. This span starts at tile row 1 and runs through row 1; the stream continues to $55AE.
Packed bytes for normal scene 04. This span continues inside tile row 1 and runs through row 10; the stream continues to $55AE.
Packed bytes for normal scene 04. This span continues inside tile row 10 and runs through row 12; the stream continues to $55AE.

Packed bytes for normal scene 08. This span continues inside tile row 8 and runs through row 12; the stream continues to $6BCD.
The unpacker transfers control here. The jump over the build dedication enters start-up at $75F9.
Programmer's dedication and TBA C64 V1.0 identification, skipped by the jump at $6D00.
Palette selection indexed by tile number. $7E28 uses the next map column's tile IDs to colour the incoming character columns.
Per-scene colour set at $8690 for tile $01.
Palette value patched by $8685 for tile $07.
First of the five entries assigned the colour selected by $8647.
Palette slot for tile $10. Scene initialization assigns the shared colour for this group at $8685.
Palette slot for tile $11. Scene initialization assigns the shared colour for this group at $8685.
Palette slot for tile $12. Scene initialization assigns the shared colour for this group at $8685.
Colour slot patched by $8685 as part of the group which takes one common colour per scene.
Colour entry for tile $21, set from the scene-specific table at $8655.
Palette slot for tile $6E. Scene initialization assigns the shared colour for this group at $8685.
Palette slot for tile $6F. Scene initialization assigns the shared colour for this group at $8685.
Palette slot for tile $70. Scene initialization assigns the shared colour for this group at $8685.
The final colour slot of the four redefined together at $86BA-$86C3.
Palette value patched by $8685 for tile $79.
Zero selects the normal scene index. Values $0C and $0D select the bonus and secret map streams.
Tile $7E starts this counter. The update at $B92C switches to the secret map at its observed value five.
Rock count. The tile handler at $9E13 increments it and the fire handler at $9930 decrements it.
Six decimal accumulators from least to most significant. $8033 propagates decimal carries and redraws them.
Nonzero selects the rock launch path and the corresponding weapon sprite.
One-bit animation phase toggled by $C192. It decides whether the even row is solid in the handler at $C173.
Signed movement accumulator updated by joystick direction and braking. Its magnitude selects the requested pixel delta.
Current index into the vertical step table for the held or decaying jump state.
Six digits against which $C32A compares the score from its most significant end.
Sprite index selected for each of the six objects, also used by the weapon and player overlap checks.
Count eligible calls to the timer routine, resetting after the fifteenth call.
Life-loss animation advances this counter. The stage-clear score tally checks it as the timer-expiration flag, while the banner waits on its separate frame-delay table.
Prevents the regular movement and weapon logic while initialization or the transition holds the player.
Zero-based regular scene number. The alternate map selector is a different byte at $6DD2.
Logical sprite index for each $6E63 platform, set by the spawn routine and reused by both motion paths.
Per-slot delta added to a platform's sprite Y by $B6D8.
Map column stored for each active $6E6B object and read for a later tile collision.
Per-slot spawn state saved by the $A1C7 allocator before writing the movement bytes at $6F94.
Secondary state saved before setting visibility for the matching $6E49 slot.
Per-slot state whose zero value sends $BCD6 into its alternate graphic-update path.
The low byte of the game's random state, seeded with $34 in the handoff image. $7E44 mixes it with the next byte.
Second byte of the random state, initialized to $3E in the handoff image and rotated by $7E44.
Software mirror for the screen and character base register, with $30 toggled when the buffers exchange.
Set to five by title fire. Its displayed digit is one less than the capped count.
Temporary per-scene sprite attribute passed in Y to $A9F1 when the new object is allocated.
Seven-byte PETSCII names in eight-byte slots. Retained LOAD path at $B608 selects the name for a scene by multiplying the scene index by eight.
Per-item sprite offsets used for writing the selected HUD glyph in $95A5.
Score digit delta selected by the hit-result routine at $964F.
Offset lookup used by $A0B6 to compute the difference between the tile column and the visible screen position.
Low bytes of character-matrix row addresses selected by $A09F.
High bytes paired with the $716F row offsets. $A0A8 adds the active matrix's page.
Phase-indexed value tested for the $FF marker in the precursor animation.
Base of the one-based sprite sequence used by $C31C to advance the tile-spawned sprite.
A zero-terminated sequence of sprite pointers used by the spawn and expiry animations and by the scene-clear animation.
Vertical movement indexed by the player's current jump or falling phase in $7AD4 and $7B2F.
Initial graphic bytes for the sprite work buffer at $0200, loaded during scene setup.
Initial graphic bytes copied into $0180 for the scene renderer.
Graphic source copied into $0240 by the scene sprite setup loop.
Graphic source copied into $0280 by the same setup loop, for the next sprite slot.
Source graphic bytes used by $C356 to build writable title display sprites.
Second source graphic array used alongside the array at $7227 in the title graphics setup.
Forty-eight graphic bytes copied to $0240 by $C455.
Forty-eight graphic bytes copied to $0280 by $C45B.
The $A835 trigger cursor starts at this scene-indexed offset before $8512 scans toward the camera.
Initial cursor offset used by the scene event-list scan at $85DA for this object's trigger list.
Scene-indexed initial cursor used at $8616 before advancing toward the initial camera column.
Scene-indexed offset used at $85EE to seek this event list.
$8587 reads this scene's initial offset into the corresponding trigger list.
$859B selects the initial event index from this table before comparing positions with the camera.
Cursor start for the next event group in the scene setup scan.
Per-scene offsets into an event-column list. The scan finds the first eligible entry at or after the starting map column.
Scene-indexed initial offset into the $A3C3 column list.
Start offset into $A125 for the scene scan at $853A.
Scene-indexed base used when the event cursor is prepared.
Index into the $B64F list of platform columns, selected in scene setup.
Map trigger offset into the $AA37 column list.
Scene-indexed starting cursor for the $A75E event columns.
Initial timer hundreds by checkpoint selected in $8238-$8273.
Initial timer tens by checkpoint. Units are cleared by the caller.
Twelve groups of four tile columns. The three non-initial entries establish the scene's checkpoint boundaries.
The comparison at $8241 starts at the second byte of each scene's checkpoints. The routine picks one of four columns according to the player's saved position.
Twelve groups of four spawn tile rows, indexed with the same scene and checkpoint as the column table.
One byte per physical sprite, with its X high bit clear and the other seven bits set.
One byte per physical sprite, with its own X high bit set.
Return carry clear to the probing caller without changing tile state.
Return carry set so the probing caller can resolve the solid tile contact.

For the player, require no active transition, no $6EDA flag and within-cell Y of at least six before setting both transition flags. For other objects return the result of comparing their slot with $10.
Unconditional carry-set return used by the tile dispatch table.
Use grid-row parity for the player or the saved row parity for an object. The tile is solid on the odd character row.
Compare selector 3 with $6E13. Carry is clear on equality.
Compare selector 2 with $6E13. Carry is clear on equality.
Compare selector 1 with $6E13. Carry is clear on equality.
Compare selector zero with $6E13. Carry is clear on equality.
Set the scene-complete and movement-inhibit flags for Terry if $6E21 is set, no finish is active, and player Y equals $A0. Return solid.
Return carry set when X is at least $10, clear otherwise.
Require Terry, a live scene, and enough depth inside the cell before checking the horizontal offset and probe direction. Set both transition flags when those tests pass, then return carry clear.
Return carry set for objects. For Terry, return carry set on the even row while the within-row offset is below four.
On a qualifying player probe, clear the display cells, write tile $54 to the map and allocate an object sprite with pointer $D8.
For Terry with $7091 clear and an odd character row, continue through the offset and direction checks at $746E.
Consume this tile through $9EC1. On a successful consume, increment score digit $6DFB and return carry clear.
For Terry when no transition is active, increment the transition counter and the $6E1B death variant flag. Return carry clear.
128 little-endian function pointers. The map read doubles the low-seven-bit tile ID, and the player and object dispatchers patch their jump operands from the corresponding table entry.
High byte of vector zero. Because the dispatchers index both bytes with twice the tile ID, later bytes continue the interleaved vector table.
Copy the 128-byte seed at $0EC0 to $1F00 for scene setup and install the start-up values at $384B and six addresses in the $1C00 tile tables.
Blank the display, clear both character matrices, reset the stack and bank out BASIC and KERNAL. Reset flags, load the first resident map, set up raster interrupts, then enter the attract loop.
Wait four IRQ ticks between iterations. Cycles sprite visibility bits and polls for fire. On the eight-bit timer wrap, flags a demonstration and continues to scene setup.
Turn off the attract display, reset stage and score state, reset the graphics drawing state and enter scene initialization.
Set up the scene and select the audio mode according to the demonstration flag and bonus-scene selector. Seed the SID volume used by the pause control.
Scan the keyboard matrix, allowing RUN/STOP to return to the attract screen. Run the routine group for each eligible IRQ-driven flag and mark it serviced before running the group.
Read CIA1 port A bit 4. Held fire clears the demonstration flag, writes five to the life counter and returns carry set. Otherwise return carry clear.

Throttle keyboard checks to every eight IRQ ticks. One matrix combination mutes the SID and sets the pause flag; a direction clears it and restores volume. Other matrix combinations select weapon mode or branch to a reset path.
Write Y as the matrix row mask to CIA1 port A, compare the requested byte in A against port B, and return the compare flags.
Set the grids at $0400 and $0800, including the rest of their four-page areas, to character zero.
Write the same A value to all four pages at $D800-$DBFF using an indexed loop.
Add A to the IRQ tick at $A2, then spin until $A2 equals the saved result. The addition and comparison use eight-bit values.
Clear the display enable shadow and write $03 to VIC control 1. Wait until raster reaches at least line $FE while its ninth bit is clear.
Poll the VIC raster high bit in $D011 and then the low byte in $D012, restarting the test until an eligible line is reached.
Call the raster wait, decrement X and repeat until it reaches zero.
Write $13 to VIC control 1 and return.
Main playfield background for each regular scene and alternate selector, written to the shadow of $D021.
Scene-indexed colour saved to the shadow of $D022.
Scene-indexed colour saved to the shadow of $D023.
Scene-indexed sprite multicolour value written to $D025 in scene setup.

Save A, X and Y by patching the restore operands at $7E8D, $7E8F and $7E91. Increment the frame tick, run the music player when enabled, establish the playfield palette and scroll, and schedule the first sprite interrupt at line 42.
If the character-boundary flag is set, toggle $30 in the VIC matrix register shadow, publish it, and update the colour column. Clear the flag after the exchange.
Collect live or demonstration direction bits, then compute the player's movement for this frame unless the scene flags inhibit it.
Add a pixel delta to the fine-scroll counter. A result of eight or more wraps by eight, requests a screen swap and advances the subcolumn. Three subcolumns advance the 24-pixel map column.
Convert the nonnegative momentum magnitude in Y to a pixel delta in $70B0. Intermediate speeds use the low bit of the frame tick to alternate the step between adjacent integers.
Copy the requested run of columns across 24 rows from the visible matrix to its alternate. The caller fills the newly exposed column in the destination.
Read one map tile per row from $1000 and then each following page. Use the tile index and subcolumn to choose the two character codes that enter the screen at the final column of that row pair.
Maps the three subcolumn phases to the offsets used by the colour scroll.
Use the subcolumn phase to update the colour RAM columns for the current display shift.
When the subcolumn phase reaches two, read the next map column's tile IDs and write their palette selection on both cells of the rightmost character column in each of twelve row pairs.
Rotate and XOR the low byte of a two-byte state, rotate its neighbouring byte and save the next low byte. Callers mask its result for bounded chance decisions.
Immediate operand patched with the interrupted accumulator by $797C and read back during the return.
Immediate operand patched with the interrupted X register by $797F.
Immediate operand patched with the interrupted Y register by $7982.
Consult the trigger bytes for the current map column and call the corresponding spawn routines. At subcolumn zero, also check the map for tile-triggered objects.
Ten glyphs of eight bytes each, ordered 0 through 9. Code at $7FE6 copies one glyph down a byte column of an eight-row sprite section.
Offset 1 into each eight-byte digit bitmap. $9DA1 uses it to construct a numeral in the auxiliary sprite slots.
Offset 3 into each eight-byte digit bitmap. $9DA1 uses it to construct a numeral in the auxiliary sprite slots.
Offset 4 into each eight-byte digit bitmap. $9DA1 uses it to construct a numeral in the auxiliary sprite slots.
Offset 6 into each eight-byte digit bitmap. $9DA1 uses it to construct a numeral in the auxiliary sprite slots.
Last bitmap row of the first HUD digit. Subsequent rows here belong to digits 1 through 9.
Skip the countdown while the transition counter or $A1 is set. Otherwise increment a prescaler and subtract one displayed unit on its fifteenth call.
Subtract from the units digit and borrow through the tens and hundreds on underflow. If hundreds underflows, clamp all three to zero and set the two transition flags.
The second digit-decrement opcode. On underflow, reset tens using the current value in A and continue into hundreds.
The final digit-decrement opcode, also writable by the routine at $FC68. On underflow, clear all three timer digits and start the transition.
Draw the hundreds, tens and units digits into adjacent byte columns of the HUD sprite.
Multiply the digit in A by eight. Copy eight bytes from the glyph table to $0C00 plus Y with a stride of three, one byte per VIC sprite row.
Convert the bonus digit to an eight-byte glyph offset. Copy its rows into sprite memory at $2400 plus the current column offset.
Six offsets locating the byte columns for the score digit glyphs.
Test all six stored digit positions and skip the score update only when every byte is zero.
Walk six score positions, carrying excess units into the more significant positions, and write the digit graphics to their HUD sprite columns.
Preserve X and Y, cap the displayed life count at nine, subtract one and send it to the HUD digit writer.
Assign logical slots two and three sprite pointers $30 and $31. Set their X values 24 pixels apart with the same Y and colour.
Sprite images selected during the life-loss countdown at $80E5.
Increment the transition counter and select an animation action according to the previous count. At the final phase, either decrement lives and restart the scene, or return to the title.

After the death sequence, decrement lives unless the preceding branch skips this instruction. If lives remain, clear transient scene flags and restart. Otherwise run the game-over display and return to attract.
Clear Terry's visible sprite, make the Game Over text using sprite pointers $39/$3A, update the best score and play the selected tune for the end delay.
Halt the display, reset scene input and rendering flags, silence and initialize sound, clear the matrices and establish the new map and sprite state.
Set the HUD sprite graphics and object palette, choose camera and spawn setup using the scene and checkpoint indices, draw the first section of the map, and enable the visible scene.
Add two to the bonus time state, cap the result at six and set the tens digit. Clear the hundreds and the saved bonus time state.
Logical sprite attributes copied to the first byte of each sprite record at interlude setup.
Source sprite indices copied to the image field of each new setup sprite.
Low coordinates used for the first placement of the setup sprites.
High X coordinates paired with the $82FB table.
Initial Y coordinates paired with the setup sprite records.
Clear or restore scene setup buffers. Use the regular scene index, or the bonus selector for an alternate map, before calling the resident map decoder.
Copy one eight-row glyph from the table indexed by X to one byte column at $0306 plus Y, advancing by three bytes per sprite row.
Clear the temporary scene-label data in the sprite area at $0EC0.
Starting byte of the short selection-coordinate lookup at $845E. Active direction indices choose its second or third byte.
Y coordinate compared at $8470 to select scene zero.
Poll port 2 Up and Down to change Terry's selection position. Fire commits either scene zero or the stored scene at $6EA2, according to the resulting vertical position.
Scroll Terry's setup sprites and a run of scenery objects four pixels at a time, change walking poses and wait one frame per iteration. X selects the first other sprite and Y the number of steps.
Populate the entering edge's colour RAM, then set the IRQ-driven delay to $28 and wait until it reaches zero.

For a regular scene, use the scene's start offsets for multiple event lists, advance each until its column is at or beyond the camera column, and store the cursor and inverted column for later trigger checks.
$8685 selects a value for the tile $01 colour entry at $6D49.
The replacement colour for tile $07, stored at $6D4F.
Value used for five tile-colour entries at $6D56 and $6D58-$6D5B.
Matrix palette value for tile $21 at $6D69.
Common scene colour assigned to four tile entries $6DB6 through $6DB9.
Palette for tile $79, installed in $6DC1 before drawing.
Six character codes copied as a unit into the definition at $1C84.
Select the normal or alternate map index and copy its palette entries to the tile colour table. Then copy six selected character codes to $1C84.
Wait at the end of the raster and clear the logical sprite records starting at $02.
Clear the sound registers at $D400 through $D417 with an indexed store loop.
Map prepared sprite Y to the scheduler's raster band number. $8801 uses the sixteen logical positions as indices.
Final 24 bytes of the Y-indexed band table share the same bucket value $11.

Prepare the displayed X and Y values, colours and band membership for the sixteen logical sprite slots. The raster-band handler uses the prepared values so it can fill VIC slots without sorting coordinates in its time-critical pass.

Process sixteen logical sprite buckets against the current raster band. For each matching bucket, publish X, Y, X high bit, colour and image pointer to the next physical sprite, descending from 7 through 0 and wrapping.
Advance the band and add 40 to its raster line. At $F2 hand off to the bottom-border interrupt. Store the vector in RAM and acknowledge the VIC interrupt.
Restore immediate operands from the most recent interrupt entry and return from interrupt. The entry writes those operand bytes at $8EBF, $8EC1 and $8EC3.
Immediate operand patched with the accumulator by the sprite band handler's entry.
Immediate operand patched with X at the sprite band handler's entry.
Immediate operand patched with Y at the sprite band handler's entry.
Prepare the bottom display, clear the playfield background and sprite coordinates, and schedule the next frame handler through the hardware vector.
Find an available logical sprite slot starting at the object area in zero page; carry signals that the scan found no free slot.
Derive an X placement from the shifted slot index and a smaller spacing adjustment, with a threshold correction at $3A.
Apply the signed movement delta to the within-column X position. Borrow across a 24-pixel map tile boundary when the result is negative.
Apply the positive movement delta to the within-column X position. Carry into the next tile column at 24 pixels.
Subtract the requested Y step from the within-row coordinate, borrowing from the character row in steps of eight pixels.
Add the requested Y step to the within-row coordinate and wrap into the next character row at eight pixels.
Resolve a character-row coordinate to a map row page, use the coarse player column as index, and double the tile ID for the collision vector table. Bytes with the high bit set are treated as zero.
Resolve object character-row and map column to a tile handler index. It converts an out-of-bounds row, a consumed tile or a disabled $54 tile to index zero.
Tile ID fetched at $9013 and normalized before being doubled for dispatch.
Select the tile row using the current weapon movement coordinate, save parity, and double the map tile ID at the weapon column for dispatch.
Compute overlap between the weapon bounds and the candidate logical object in X. Carry indicates an overlap.

Skip unless the weapon is active. Derive bounds from its sprite position, then scan the active-object tables with per-group sizes and reactions. Dispatch into score or hit handling when the weapon connects.
An RTS byte between the weapon-hit JMP at $919A and the next hit path.
Process the remaining active-object pools, calling the same overlap check with each pool's sprite slot. Update or clear a candidate's state and branch to the shared hit effects.
